hero_summary.headline: Your emotional system is generally stable and is usually not easily pulled up significantly by short-term fluctuations.
hero_summary.body_core: You are less susceptible to stress, misunderstandings, and uncertainties, making it easier to maintain a stable baseline.

domains_overview.snapshot_line: When your stress response sensitivity is low, you are more likely to remain stable in uncertainty, but you also need to retain awareness of early risks.

domain_deep_dive.definition: Emotional sensitivity reflects the intensity of your reaction to stress, judgment, uncertainty, and feelings of loss of control.
strengths: Not easily disrupted by short-term stimulation
Better able to maintain the original rhythm amidst fluctuations
costs: May be late in noticing subtle tensions in relationships and environments
Easier to underestimate early consumption signals of a problem
domain_deep_dive.daily_life: You generally won't stall significantly quickly due to ambiguity and uncertainty.

core_portrait.identity: Your emotional system is more homeostatic.
core_portrait.default_style: You can usually maintain a relatively stable pace of reaction to external fluctuations.

norms_comparison.relative_meaning: In the reference sample, the intensity of your stress response was relatively undistinguished, closer to a low-volatility emotional baseline.

action_plan.priority_hint: Your immediate focus is more on maintaining risk sensitivity than on repairing overload.

hero_summary.headline: Your emotional system fluctuates depending on the situation, but it is not constantly on high alert.
hero_summary.body_core: In situations of high pressure, misunderstandings, and blurred boundaries, you will feel significantly more physical, but you will usually still be able to gradually return to a steady state.

domains_overview.snapshot_line: With stress response sensitivity in the middle, you can usually feel the tension, but whether you're taken away depends on context intensity and recovery tempo.

domain_deep_dive.definition: Emotional sensitivity determines the intensity of your feelings of stress, judgment, uncertainty, and relationship tension.
strengths: Have a real sense of risk and what’s wrong
Not easy to pass over problems in a dull manner
Ability to detect changes in environmental quality earlier
costs: Load will gradually accumulate under repeated pulling situations
domain_deep_dive.daily_life: You don’t necessarily show it on the spot, but the cost is already starting to be borne internally.

core_portrait.identity: You are not a person who is constantly on high alert, but your system will clearly ripple in certain situations.
core_portrait.default_style: You have a real sense of environmental quality and relationship tension.

norms_comparison.relative_meaning: In the reference sample, your stress response intensity is mid-range sensitive, more like a conditioned high body sensation.

action_plan.priority_hint: Your focus is to upgrade the recovery after the wave from "natural fallback" to "conscious adjustment."

hero_summary.headline: Your emotional system is highly sensitive - this is both an early warning and a cost.
hero_summary.body_core: You feel something is wrong earlier than many people, and you are more likely to suffer from obvious internal friction in blurred boundaries, repeated misunderstandings and uncertainty.

domains_overview.snapshot_line: When your stress response sensitivity is high, you capture risks and relationship tensions earlier, and you have a greater need to put your recovery mechanism in front of you.

domain_deep_dive.definition: Emotional sensitivity determines how strongly you respond to stress, risk, evaluation, uncertainty, and feelings of loss of control.
strengths: Easier to detect changes in relationships and environment
It’s not easy to be dull and ignore small cracks
costs: Easier to bring external tension back inside
It’s easier to bear the psychological cost before things break out
domain_deep_dive.daily_life: It’s not that you don’t have the ability, but you need recovery mechanisms, boundaries and a stable rhythm to support the intensity of your reaction.

core_portrait.identity: Your feeling system is strong, your early warning system is strong, and your internal load is also strong.
core_portrait.default_style: You know something is wrong earlier, and you pay the psychological cost earlier.

norms_comparison.relative_meaning: In the reference sample, the intensity of your stress response is more prominent, which means that you are more naturally living in a high somatosensory warning mode.

action_plan.priority_hint: Your key issue is not to "don't be sensitive", but to not let your sensitivity stay internal for a long time.
